FUTURES FUNDING FAQS
What is Goat Funded Futures?

GOAT Funded Futures (GFF) is a futures proprietary trading firm that provides traders with simulated funded accounts to trade CME, COMEX, NYMEX, and CBOT listed futures products.

We offer a variety of plans: GOAT Daily, the EOD Challenge, the Flex Challenge and the 1-Day-Pass-Plan (evaluation-based), plus Instant (no evaluation required).

How do futures prop firms work?

Futures prop firms give traders access to accounts under a defined set of trading rules. Many require an evaluation, where traders must reach a profit target without exceeding drawdown limits. Others offer instant funding plans. At Goat Funded Futures, the route depends on the plan you choose. Each plan sets out the account type, trading rules, reward requirements and profit split.

What funding plans does Goat Funded Futures offer?

Goat Funded Futures offers GOAT Daily, Flex, EOD, 1-Day Pass and Instant plans. The evaluation plans require traders to meet the relevant targets before progressing to a funded account. The Instant plan skips the evaluation stage.

How much does an evaluation cost?

The evaluation fee depends on your plan and account size. For example, a $50K GOAT Daily evaluation is listed at $198 (pre-discount), with no activation fee after passing and reset fees from $90. See the pricing table for current prices and discounts.

What does the evaluation involve?

During an evaluation, you trade a simulated account and aim to reach the profit target while staying within the plan's trading rules. For GOAT Daily, during the evaluation, no single day can account for more than 40% or 50% of your total profit, depending on the option you choose at checkout. Once funded, there is no consistency rule. Once you meet the requirements, you can progress to a funded account.

Rules vary between plans, so check the requirements for your chosen account before purchasing.

What are the drawdown types and main trading rules?

There are two drawdown types depending on the plan: End of Day trailing drawdown (EOD, Flex, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Instant and GOAT Daily during the evaluation), which updates only at the close of each trading day so your intraday swings have room, and intraday trailing drawdown (GOAT Daily funded accounts), which updates in real time. On the 1-Day-Pass-Plan the End of Day drawdown locks at the starting balance. Core rules apply across all plans: no holding positions overnight or over the weekend, and a 2 minute buffer around high impact news events on funded accounts (on GOAT Daily, in both phases). Daily Loss Limits and consistency requirements vary by plan: for example EOD has a funded daily loss limit, while on GOAT Daily, Flex, the 1-Day-Pass-Plan and Instant the daily loss limit is optional at checkout. If selected, hitting it closes the account.

How does the profit split work?

It depends on the plan. GOAT Daily uses a 90/10 split from your first reward. EOD, the 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex and Instant use an 80/20 split by default, with 90/10 available as a paid add-on. The split is simply applied to the profit you withdraw, with no hidden conditions. A 3% processing fee is deducted from every reward.

How fast do I receive my rewards?

We back our rewards with a guarantee: once you request a reward, it is processed within 2 business days (within 48 hours on GOAT Daily). If your reward ever takes longer than that, you receive an extra $500 as a reward. Rewards can be requested via stablecoin (USDC / USDT) and bank transfer where available, with a $500 minimum. A 3% processing fee is deducted from every reward.

Which trading platforms can I use?

Goat Funded Futures lists NinjaTrader, Tradovate, TradingView (via Tradovate), TickBlaze, DeepCharts, ATAS, Tradesea and WealthCharts. Check the platform information for supported connections, market data arrangements and any setup requirements before choosing.

Can I hold trades during news events?

Yes, during the evaluation phase news trading is unrestricted while you work to pass your challenge, except on GOAT Daily. On funded accounts, and on GOAT Daily in both phases, a 2 minute buffer applies around high impact news events, meaning you cannot open, close, or trigger pending orders within 2 minutes before or after a scheduled release. This lets you trade your strategy while keeping conditions fair once you are on funded capital.

AFFILIATE FAQ
How do I join the affiliate program?

Apply with the form on this page. Our team reviews every application. Once you're approved, you get your affiliate link and your invite link in your affiliate dashboard.

How much commission do I earn?

Tier 1: 12% on every sale, from your first customer until you have referred 99 unique customers.

Tier 2: 15% on every sale from your 100th unique customer onward, and it stays yours permanently.

The count is based on different customers, not purchases. There is no separate rate for your first sale.

Which purchases count toward my commission?

We use a 30-day cookie: every purchase made within 30 days of a click on your link earns you commission, including repeat purchases by the same customer.

Challenge purchases and add-ons earn commission, resets don't. Commission is calculated on the price the customer paid, after any discount. Your own purchases don't earn commission.

What are sub-affiliates?

Invite other creators, influencers or traders to apply with the invite link in your dashboard. Everyone who is approved through it becomes your sub-affiliate, and you earn 5% of every sale they make, for as long as their affiliate account stays active.

There is no limit on how many sub-affiliates you can invite. The 5% covers one level only.

Does my 5% reduce my sub-affiliates' commission?

No. Your sub-affiliates keep their full 12% or 15% on their sales. Your 5% is paid on top and never comes out of their commission.

How do custom coupons work?

You can create up to 5 personalised coupons from your dashboard, with a discount of up to 40%. Purchases made with your coupon count for you even outside the 30-day cookie window, and you can also give your coupons to your sub-affiliates.

What is the $10K milestone?

Reach $10,000 in attributed sales to receive a $500 cash bonus and GFF Ambassador status, with Ambassador perks, giveaways and other benefits.

When can I request my commission?

Each commission can be requested 30 days after it's credited to your account. The minimum request is $100, and identity verification (KYC) is required before your first request. Commissions are sent by crypto or Skrill and usually take 2 days to process.

What happens with refunds and chargebacks?

If a sale you referred is refunded or charged back, the commission on it is removed, even after its 30 days. If it was already paid, it's deducted from your balance.

Affiliate Program

Updated 14 November 2026Copy link

You earn commission on every sale made through your affiliate link. You also earn 5% of the sales made by affiliates you invite, called sub-affiliates.

How to join
Copy link

Apply on our Affiliate Program page. Our team reviews every application. Once you're approved, you'll get your affiliate link and your invite link.

Your commission
Copy link
12% on your sales until you have referred 100 different customers.
15% on every sale from your 100th customer onward.

The 100 counts different customers, not purchases. If one customer buys three accounts within 30 days of clicking your link, each purchase earns commission, but that customer counts once toward the 100. Customers you referred before the new rates also count.

Challenge purchases and add-ons earn commission. Resets don't.

Commission is calculated on the price the customer paid, after any discount. Your own purchases don't earn commission.

There is no separate rate for your first sale.

Sub-affiliate commission
Copy link

Invite other creators, influencers or traders to apply to the affiliate program with your invite link. Everyone who is approved after applying through it becomes your sub-affiliate, and you earn 5% of the full amount of every sale they make.

Your sub-affiliates still earn their own full 12% or 15% on those sales. Your 5% doesn't come out of their commission.

You earn the 5% for as long as your sub-affiliate's account stays active. If their affiliate account is disabled for any reason, including fraud, the 5% stops.

Someone only becomes your sub-affiliate by applying through your invite link. An affiliate who already joined without it can't be linked to you unless they apply again through your link.

There is no limit on how many sub-affiliates you can invite. The 5% covers one level only, so you don't earn on affiliates that your sub-affiliates invite.

Your invite link is in your affiliate dashboard.

Example
Copy link

Say you invite 10 creators and each of them makes $2,000 in sales this month. That's $20,000 in total, and 5% of it is $1,000 for you, without selling anything extra yourself.

SUB-AFFILIATES	SALES EACH PER MONTH	TOTAL SALES	YOUR 5%
5	$2,000	$10,000	$500
10	$2,000	$20,000	$1,000
10	$10,000	$100,000	$5,000
20	$10,000	$200,000	$10,000

If your sub-affiliates grow and sell more, your 5% grows with them.

When you can request your commission
Copy link

You can request a commission 30 days after it's credited to your account. Each commission has its own 30 days. For example, commission credited on 13 November can be requested from 13 December.

The minimum payout request is $100. You need to complete identity verification (KYC) before your first payout. Payouts are sent by crypto or Skrill and usually take 2 days to process.

Cookie tracking
Copy link

We use a 30-day cookie. If someone clicks your link and buys within 30 days, the sale counts toward your commission. Purchases after those 30 days don't count. For example, if someone clicks your link and buys on day 29 and again on day 31, only the first purchase earns commission.

Refunds and chargebacks
Copy link

If a sale you referred is refunded or charged back, the commission on it is removed, even if its 30 days have already passed. If it was already paid out, it's deducted from your balance.

We may disable the affiliate account of affiliates with a high number of refunds or chargebacks.

What is a trailing drawdown?
Copy link

A trailing drawdown is a loss level that moves upward as your account reaches new highs, but never moves back down. Think of it as a rising floor beneath your account. It follows your profits up but stays put when you give back. If your account equity falls to or below this level, the account is breached.

Once the drawdown floor reaches its lock point, it stays there permanently and stops trailing. This applies to all account types, both challenges and funded accounts. On most plans the lock point is your initial starting balance. On Daily Payouts and Instant (Instant Lite included) it is your starting balance plus $100.

There are two types of trailing drawdown at GOAT Funded Futures.

Trailing EOD (end of day)Copy link

Used on EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex and Instant accounts (Instant Lite included), and on Daily Payouts during the evaluation. The drawdown floor only updates at the end of each trading day, based on your closing balance.

Example (50K account, $2,000 max drawdown):

You start at $50,000, so your floor is $48,000.
You close the day at $51,500, so your floor moves up to $49,500.
During the next day your equity dips to $49,200 intraday but you close at $50,800. No breach, because the floor is based on your end of day balance, not intraday equity.
Over time, your closing balances push the floor up to $50,000, your initial starting balance. The floor is now locked and will not trail any further.
Trailing intradayCopy link

Used on Daily Payouts funded accounts, and on Instant Classic accounts bought before 18 November 2026. The drawdown floor updates in real time, tracking your highest equity point during the session, including unrealised profits on open positions.

Example (50K account, $2,000 max drawdown):

You start at $50,000, so your floor is $48,000.
Your equity reaches $51,500 during a trade, so your floor moves up to $49,500 immediately.
If your equity drops to $49,500 at any point, even before closing the trade, the account is breached.
Your equity continues climbing to $52,000, so the floor moves to $50,000, your initial starting balance. The floor is now locked and will not trail any further.
Daily Payouts uses bothCopy link

The evaluation runs end of day trailing and the funded account switches to intraday trailing. See the Daily Payouts drawdown article.

Important note for funded accountsCopy link

Once the drawdown floor locks, your account has very little cushion below that level. For example, if you have grown your 50K account to $54,000 and withdraw $4,000 in profits, your balance returns to $50,000, which is exactly where the floor is locked. At that point any drop in equity at all will breach the account. Always keep a buffer in your account when making withdrawals.

Updated 19 November 2026

What is the difference between EOD trailing and intraday trailing drawdown?
Copy link

The key difference is when the drawdown floor updates.

EOD trailing drawdownCopy link

Used on EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex and Instant accounts (Instant Lite included), and on Daily Payouts during the evaluation.

The drawdown floor only updates at the end of each trading day, based on your closing balance. Intraday equity swings do not affect your drawdown level.

For example, if your account peaks at $52,000 during the session but closes at $50,500, the drawdown floor adjusts based on $50,500 only.

Intraday trailing drawdownCopy link

Used on Daily Payouts funded accounts, and on Instant Classic accounts bought before 18 November 2026.

The drawdown floor updates in real time as your equity reaches new highs, including unrealised profits on open positions. If your equity hits $52,000 even momentarily, the drawdown floor adjusts immediately and never moves back down.

Daily Payouts uses bothCopy link

The evaluation runs end of day trailing, and the funded account switches to intraday trailing on your highest equity. See the Daily Payouts drawdown article for what changes when you get funded.

How does intraday trailing drawdown work?
Copy link

The Maximum Trailing Intraday Drawdown sets the lowest equity level your account is allowed to reach at any point during a trading session, including on open positions. It trails your highest equity point in real time, meaning as your account reaches new equity highs, the drawdown floor automatically moves up by the same amount. It never moves back down.

Only Daily Payouts funded accounts use intraday trailing. EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex, Instant and the Daily Payouts evaluation all use end of day trailing, where the floor is calculated from your closing balance and only updates after the trading day ends. Instant Classic accounts bought before 18 November 2026 also use intraday trailing, as in the example below.

This is important to understand: the drawdown floor tracks your highest equity, not your closing balance. Even if you give back profits before closing a trade, the floor will have already moved up.

Once the drawdown floor reaches its lock point, it stays there permanently and stops trailing. On Instant Classic the lock point is your initial starting balance. On Daily Payouts it is your starting balance plus $100.

Example (Instant Classic 50K account, $2,000 max drawdown):

Your account starts at $50,000, so the max drawdown floor is set at $48,000.
Your equity rises to $51,000 during a trade, so the floor moves up to $49,000.
If your equity drops to $49,000 at any point, the account is breached, even if the trade has not been closed.
Your equity continues climbing to $52,000, so the floor moves to $50,000, your initial starting balance. The floor is now locked and will not trail any further.
Even if your equity later reaches $55,000, the floor stays at $50,000.

On a funded Daily 50K the same mechanics apply, but the floor locks at $50,100 once your equity reaches $52,100. See the Daily Payouts drawdown article.

Important note for funded accounts: once the drawdown floor locks, your account has very little cushion below that level. For example, if you have grown your Instant Classic 50K account to $54,000 and withdraw $4,000 in profits, your balance returns to $50,000, which is exactly where the floor is locked. At that point any drop in equity at all will breach the account. Always keep a buffer in your account when making withdrawals.

What does "drawdown lock" or "DD Lock" mean?
Copy link
Important for Funded AccountsCopy link

The drawdown continues to trail normally as your account reaches new equity highs until it reaches your account's initial starting balance. Once it reaches the starting balance, it locks permanently and will not trail any higher.

On Daily Payouts, Instant and Instant Lite the lock point is your starting balance plus $100, not your starting balance. On a Daily 50K the limit locks at $50,100 once your equity reaches $52,100.

Requesting or receiving a payout does not automatically move or lock your drawdown at the starting balance. Your drawdown remains wherever it was before the payout.

Example

On a $50,000 funded account:

Current account balance: $51,000
Current drawdown floor: $49,000

If you request a $1,000 payout, your account balance becomes $50,000, but your drawdown floor remains at $49,000 because it had not yet reached the starting balance before the payout.

This means you now have $1,000 of remaining drawdown room.

Only after the drawdown naturally reaches your account's initial starting balance does it lock permanently.

Once the drawdown has locked, it will remain there even after future payouts. If your balance later falls below that level, the account will be breached.

Does requesting a payout lock my drawdown at the starting balance?Copy link

No. Requesting or receiving a payout does not change the position of your drawdown floor.

The drawdown continues to trail according to your account rules until it naturally reaches your lock point. Only then does it lock permanently.

If the drawdown has not yet reached the lock point before the payout, it will remain at its current level after the payout.

Why does my funded Daily Payouts account use intraday trailing drawdown?
Copy link

Daily Payouts uses a different drawdown method in each phase.

Evaluation: end of day trailing. Your limit moves up with your profits once, at the end of each trading day.
Funded: intraday trailing. Your limit moves up in real time, tracking your highest equity, including unrealised profit on open positions.
What changes when you get fundedCopy link

In the evaluation, an open position that runs to a large unrealised profit and then gives it back costs you nothing in drawdown terms. Only the end of day figure counts.

On the funded account, that same trade permanently raises your drawdown limit at the peak. If the position reverses, the limit stays where it moved to.

Example: Daily 50K fundedCopy link

Your drawdown is $2,000, so from a $50,000 start your limit is $48,000.

You open a position. Your equity peaks at $51,400 while the position is still open. Your limit moves immediately to $49,400 and stays there.

The trade reverses and you close it flat at $50,000. Your limit is still $49,400. You now have $600 of room, not the $2,000 you started with.

When does it stop moving?Copy link

The limit stops trailing permanently once it reaches your starting balance plus $100.

On a 50K that means once your equity touches $52,100, the limit locks at $50,100 for the life of the account. From then on it never moves again, up or down, and your account can only be closed by falling below $50,100.

EOD, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex and Instant Classic all lock at the starting balance, with no $100 added. Instant and Instant Lite use the same plus $100 lock point as Daily.

Does taking a payout move my limit?Copy link

No. Requesting and receiving a payout does not move or lock the drawdown limit. Your balance goes down by the payout amount, and the limit stays exactly where it was.

This matters most on the 25K. After a maximum $650 payout from the $26,100 minimum balance, you are at $25,450 against a floor locked at $25,100, which is $350 of room. On the 50K you would have $1,000, on the 100K $1,500, on the 150K $2,000.

How to trade with itCopy link

Two habits help:

Watch your peak equity, not your balance. The number that matters is the highest your equity has been, not where it closed.
Treat unrealised profit as spent. If a position runs $1,000 in your favour, assume $1,000 of your drawdown room has gone, because it has.

At least 50% of the amount you request must come from new profit generated since your previous approved payout.

FUTURES FUNDING FAQS
What is Goat Funded Futures?

GOAT Funded Futures (GFF) is a futures proprietary trading firm that provides traders with simulated funded accounts to trade CME, COMEX, NYMEX, and CBOT listed futures products.

We offer a variety of plans: GOAT Daily, the EOD Challenge, the Flex Challenge and the 1-Day-Pass-Plan (evaluation-based), plus Instant (no evaluation required).

How do futures prop firms work?

Futures prop firms give traders access to accounts under a defined set of trading rules. Many require an evaluation, where traders must reach a profit target without exceeding drawdown limits. Others offer instant funding plans. At Goat Funded Futures, the route depends on the plan you choose. Each plan sets out the account type, trading rules, reward requirements and profit split.

What funding plans does Goat Funded Futures offer?

Goat Funded Futures offers GOAT Daily, Flex, EOD, 1-Day Pass and Instant plans. The evaluation plans require traders to meet the relevant targets before progressing to a funded account. The Instant plan skips the evaluation stage.

How much does an evaluation cost?

The evaluation fee depends on your plan and account size. For example, a $50K GOAT Daily evaluation is listed at $198 (pre-discount), with no activation fee after passing and reset fees from $90. See the pricing table for current prices and discounts.

What does the evaluation involve?

During an evaluation, you trade a simulated account and aim to reach the profit target while staying within the plan's trading rules. For GOAT Daily, during the evaluation, no single day can account for more than 40% or 50% of your total profit, depending on the option you choose at checkout. Once funded, there is no consistency rule. Once you meet the requirements, you can progress to a funded account.

Rules vary between plans, so check the requirements for your chosen account before purchasing.

What are the drawdown types and main trading rules?

There are two drawdown types depending on the plan: End of Day trailing drawdown (EOD, Flex, 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Instant and GOAT Daily during the evaluation), which updates only at the close of each trading day so your intraday swings have room, and intraday trailing drawdown (GOAT Daily funded accounts), which updates in real time. On the 1-Day-Pass-Plan the End of Day drawdown locks at the starting balance. Core rules apply across all plans: no holding positions overnight or over the weekend, and a 2 minute buffer around high impact news events on funded accounts (on GOAT Daily, in both phases). Daily Loss Limits and consistency requirements vary by plan: for example EOD has a funded daily loss limit, while on GOAT Daily, Flex, the 1-Day-Pass-Plan and Instant the daily loss limit is optional at checkout. If selected, hitting it closes the account.

How does the profit split work?

It depends on the plan. GOAT Daily uses a 90/10 split from your first reward. EOD, the 1-Day-Pass-Plan, Flex and Instant use an 80/20 split by default, with 90/10 available as a paid add-on. The split is simply applied to the profit you withdraw, with no hidden conditions. A 3% processing fee is deducted from every reward.

How fast do I receive my rewards?

We back our rewards with a guarantee: once you request a reward, it is processed within 2 business days (within 48 hours on GOAT Daily). If your reward ever takes longer than that, you receive an extra $500 as a reward. Rewards can be requested via stablecoin (USDC / USDT) and bank transfer where available, with a $500 minimum. A 3% processing fee is deducted from every reward.

Which trading platforms can I use?

Goat Funded Futures lists NinjaTrader, Tradovate, TradingView (via Tradovate), TickBlaze, DeepCharts, ATAS, Tradesea and WealthCharts. Check the platform information for supported connections, market data arrangements and any setup requirements before choosing.

Can I hold trades during news events?

Yes, during the evaluation phase news trading is unrestricted while you work to pass your challenge, except on GOAT Daily. On funded accounts, and on GOAT Daily in both phases, a 2 minute buffer applies around high impact news events, meaning you cannot open, close, or trigger pending orders within 2 minutes before or after a scheduled release. This lets you trade your strategy while keeping conditions fair once you are on funded capital.

What changes when you move from evaluation to funded
Copy link

Less than you might expect. One rule genuinely changes:

The consistency rule starts applying. There is none during the evaluation. On a funded account, no single day may be more than 35% of your total profit for the payout period.

Everything else carries over unchanged: the end of day trailing drawdown and its lock, your maximum drawdown amount, the daily loss limit and its percentages, contract limits, news trading rules, overnight and weekend holding, and the 1 minute holding rule.

Payout rules apply from this point too, since there are no payouts during an evaluation: 80/20 by default, payouts every 5 winning days, and 50% of your available profit per request with the rest staying in the account.

If you bought the 90/10 Profit Share Add-On with your challenge, it carries over automatically. There is nothing to re-purchase. Since there are no payouts during an evaluation, the add-on only affects what you take home once you are funded.

Why does 1-Day-Pass-Plan cost more than EOD?
Copy link

A 1-Day-Pass-Plan costs more than an EOD account of the same size. What the extra buys:

No consistency rule during the evaluation. EOD applies a 50% rule throughout.
Faster payouts. 5 winning days instead of 7.
A more forgiving funded consistency rule. 35% on 1-Day-Pass-Plan against 30% on EOD, so a bigger single day is allowed.
A 25K entry size, which EOD does not offer.

Two tradeoffs worth knowing before you choose:

1-Day-Pass-Plan has an optional daily loss limit which, if chosen, also applies during the evaluation. EOD has none in the evaluation.
1-Day-Pass-Plan tops out at 100K. EOD goes to 150K.
